note_en: Chinese often doubles an adjective for vividness: 清楚 becomes 清清楚楚, as in 看得清清楚楚 "could see perfectly clearly," and 干净 becomes 干干净净 "spotlessly clean." The AABB form adds intensity much as English "crystal clear" or "spick-and-span" does, and it usually follows 得 or comes before 地, so you won't see 很 in front of it.
